Issued at 230 PM EDT Fri Aug 7 2026

Through Tonight...An inverted trough lifting northwest from the 
Bahamas and across the Florida peninsula has brought a deep plume 
of tropical moisture locally, with PWATs of 2.1-2.3" areawide. The
result has been an early start to convection, with early morning 
showers increasing in coverage into the afternoon hours. Active 
development of showers and storms will continue through the 
remainder of this afternoon into the evening hours, with PoPs 
between 60-70% areawide. Despite sufficient steering flow keeping 
activity moving westward, multiple rounds of showers and storms 
will lead to a higher risk of flooding across east central 
Florida, with rainfall accumulations of 2-4" and locally higher 
amounts possible. East central Florida remains outlooked in a 
Marginal Risk (1/4) of excessive rainfall today. Storm activity so
far has followed typical Florida summertime trends, with frequent
lightning strikes, wind gusts up to 50 mph, and heavy downpours 
the primary concerns. The environment remains supportive for this 
activity to persist through the remainder of this afternoon and 
evening. Guidance continues to favor activity overall diminishing 
across east central Florida beyond 8 PM, but persistent onshore 
flow coupled with the higher moisture means continued shower and 
isolated storm development across the local Atlantic waters is 
anticipated. Some of these showers and storms may be able to push 
onshore overnight and into early Saturday.

Saturday-Sunday...The inverted trough will continue to lift 
northwestward across the Florida peninsula and into the Gulf on 
Saturday, eventually diminishing into Sunday as the Atlantic high 
reestablishes itself as the dominant surface feature across the 
Florida peninsula. The plume of moisture associated with the 
trough will linger across the peninsula through this weekend, with
PoPs ranging between 50-70% on Saturday and 40-60% on Sunday. 
Activity on Saturday will follow a similar pattern to today, with 
southeasterly flow driving development across the local Atlantic 
waters and pushing it onshore, with increasing coverage across the
peninsula forecast through the afternoon hours. Weaker flow aloft
may lead to slower-moving activity Saturday, increasing the 
threat for localized flooding. The area remains outlooked in a 
Marginal Risk (1/4) of excessive rainfall on Saturday, with 
rainfall accumulations of 2-4" and locally higher amounts not able
to be ruled out in some spots. Sunday, shower and storm 
development will follow more of a diurnal pattern, with convection
primarily being driven by sea breeze development and intrusion 
inland as well as any additional outflow boundaries. Storm 
development will be possible each day through this weekend, though
activity looks to remain sub-severe overall. Cannot rule out a 
stronger storm or two on Sunday thanks to some drier air aloft 
drifting towards the area. Frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts 
of 45 to 55 mph, and heavy downpours remain the primary hazards. 
Each evening and into the overnight hours, anticipate activity 
gradually winding down with mostly dry conditions areawide.

Temperatures will overall remain near normal through this 
weekend, with highs in the upper 80s to low 90s though some 
locations near and north of the I-4 corridor could see some 
temperatures reaching the mid 90s. Humid conditions will keep peak
heat indices in the 100- 107F range this weekend, so be sure to 
remain adequately hydrated and take breaks indoors or in the shade
if staying outdoors for extended periods of time. Lows remain in 
the mid 70s.

Monday-Thursday (previous)...Atlantic ridge axis shifts back 
south across the area into early next week, and then slowly shifts
farther south of the area by mid to late week as a frontal trough
pushes into the Southeast United States. This will gradually veer
low level winds from the southeast Monday to the south-southeast 
Tuesday and then out of the west-southwest Wednesday into 
Thursday. However, winds remain weak and the east coast sea breeze
will still form and move inland each day. Mid level ridge shifts 
westward across the state and remains firmly in place through much
of next week. This combined with advection of drier air will lead
to lower than normal rain chances into next week. Forecast PoPs 
are currently no more than 20-30% for each afternoon/evening. With
coverage of showers and storms remaining isolated to scattered 
each day and with ridge in place, temperatures will continue to 
rise, with highs in the low to mid 90s each day. Will have to 
monitor for any Heat Advisories as peak heat index values may have
the potential to rise to 108-110 in some spots.
